gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the whole solar-skimmer field as of today with the plug-in backup charger counted. Counted that way: WYBOT F1 is $319.97 ($299.98 robot plus a $19.99 charger sold separately). Aiper EcoSurfer S2 is $369.99 on Amazon and comes with a DC charger. Beatbot iSkim is $359 on Amazon, not the ~$339 ChatGPT showed, and its adapter is a $25 add-on, so it costs $384. Betta SE Plus is $389.90 with an adapter. The $369.90 Betta SE has no adapter option at all, because Betta's charger is listed only for the SE Plus and Neo.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited. The Hook Up comparison and recommendation pages (both 2026-08-21) give MSRP and 'common price' for iSkim ($429/$339), EcoSurfer S2 ($399.99/$339.99), Supclean S5 ($398.99/$224.99) and Betta Neo ($429.90). They note the iSkim's $25 wall charger but list no Betta SE, SE Plus or WYBOT F1 and give no date for the prices. robotdoorstep.com (2026-11-06) prices iSkim $339, Surfer S2 $339.99 and F1 $299.98, with price dates that disagree within the page (Oct 29, Nov 1 and Nov 6). It says the F1's DC charger is sold separately but gives no charger price, and it leaves out all Betta models. Parts of the finding are already on those pages: the iSkim's $25 adapter and the F1's separate charger. What's new is today's prices across 7 models, the iSkim at $359/$379 rather than $339, the F1 charger's $19.99 price, and the fact that the Betta SE cannot be plugged in at all.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. Every name-brand solar skimmer costs $299.98 to $429.90 today, so price alone doesn't separate them. It does correct ChatGPT's '~$339' for the iSkim: it's $359 at Amazon, $384 with the adapter. It also makes WYBOT F1 the cheapest name-brand option even with its charger added ($319.97). For a shopper who means 'never plug in' literally, the Betta SE ($369.90) is the only model built that way. That cuts both ways: the SE has no backup after cloudy days, and the SE Plus adds an adapter for $20 more ($389.90).
candidates: WYBOT S2 Solar Vision (floor robot, not a skimmer)
